newsitem.title: USA: UNC comfortable with Q4, year estimates.
newsitem.headline: UNC comfortable with Q4, year estimates.

text.p: UNC Inc Chief Executive Dan Colussy said Friday he was comfortable with analysts' consensus earnings estimates of $0.15 a share for the fourth quarter and $0.35 for the full year 1996.
In a telephone interview with Reuters, Colussy said he expects revenues for UNC's manufacturing sector to grow about 25 percent in the next year.
Revenues should grow about 10 percent for the business aviation sector, and about five percent for the military aviation unit, he said.
"We're seeing the fastest growth in the manufacturing sector. We're in the first year of a five- or six-year upward cycle in airline manufacturing," Colussy said.
The business aviation sector has a "good growth thrust" and should generate revenues of $550-$600 million in 1997, he said.

The military aviation division's growth is restrained by a slow increase in outsourcing by the Pentagon. "The military sector is somewhat restrained by political battles... but there's a gravitation toward more outsourcing," Colussy said.
UNC, which acquired Stearns Co in October and Garrett Aviation Services in May, does not have any immediate plans for future acquisitions, he said.
Instead, it will expand cautiously, bolstering capacity in line with new contracts.
"We don't want to overexpand our capacity so much that we get in trouble in a downturn," he said.
UNC, which overhauls aircraft engines and manufactures jet components, employs about 7,000 workers.
